no_duplicated_code.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Duplicated Code smell?

criteria.pass: Domain rules, validation checks, error mappings, and persistence or transformation blocks are factored cleanly without copy-pasted logic across functions, branches, or files.
criteria.fail: Substantially similar validation logic, business rules, control-flow blocks, or query/mapping fragments are copy-pasted in multiple places instead of being unified into a shared helper or owning domain method.

no_long_functions.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Long Function smell, judging each individual function, method, or callback by its own inline executable logic?

criteria.pass: Each executable function, method, or callback stays concise and focused on a cohesive level of abstraction, delegating substantial implementation mechanics to well-named helpers, collaborators, or domain methods. Cohesive workflow, boundary, transaction, streaming, and orchestration functions (including concise transaction or resource-scoped callbacks) pass when they sequence calls to named helpers or collaborators with clear step ordering. A single cohesive algorithm—such as a bounded parser, converter, or projection function with brief preparation or normalization—also passes even if moderately long when its logic belongs together as one unified operation. Do not fail solely for overall file or class size, supporting type or interface declarations, declarative UI or markup composition, formatting or static literals, or an enclosing container that defines multiple short, independently triggered handlers or lifecycle callbacks.
criteria.fail: One or more individual executable functions, methods, or callbacks are long monolithic bodies that embed at least two distinct substantial implementation phases inline (such as writing out parsing, validation rules, policy calculations, state mutations, retry or I/O loops, and persistence or output formatting directly inside one function) where extracting named helpers is warranted to clarify intent and reduce nesting. A concise coordinator that sequences calls to named helpers or collaborators—even across several workflow steps or inside a short transaction callback—or a single cohesive bounded algorithm (such as a parser, converter, or projection with brief preparation) does NOT fail.

no_long_parameter_lists_or_data_clumps.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Long Parameter List and Data Clumps smells, judging only signatures declared in the supplied file and counting each declared formal parameter once?

criteria.pass: Declared function, method, and constructor signatures keep positional parameter lists concise and clear, grouping related inputs into a cohesive request, options, props, value, or context record when more inputs are needed. Count each declared formal parameter once: destructuring fields from a single object or record parameter is 1 parameter, not N, and a cohesive input/options/props record may legitimately hold many related fields. Calling an imported or external function with many arguments does not fail a caller whose own declared signatures are clean. Coincidental primitive-type reuse or a single forwarding call is not a data clump.
criteria.fail: A function, method, or constructor declared in the supplied file has an awkward sprawling positional parameter list where related inputs belong in a request, value, or context owner (especially with optional/defaulted or confusable same-type positions), OR declares a catch-all input record that genuinely mixes unrelated responsibilities across distinct callers, OR repeats the same semantic cluster of loose parameters across multiple distinct declared signatures instead of modeling a cohesive value type. Do NOT fail a signature solely because a single cohesive input/options/props record is destructured into multiple local bindings, or because the file calls an imported callee that has a wide signature.

no_feature_envy_or_data_class_anemia.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Feature Envy and anemic Data Class smells?

criteria.pass: Domain behavior, invariant checks, policy rules, and state transitions live with the owning domain types or domain modules rather than being computed externally. Both OOP domain classes with methods and idiomatic functional domain modules—where a `readonly` record or discriminated union type is colocated with pure domain query and state-transition functions—pass. Immutable read projections, boundary request/response DTOs, and persistence or UI adapters that delegate policy to owning domain operations may remain simple data carriers.
criteria.fail: External services, controllers, coordinators, transaction handlers, or unrelated helpers repeatedly reach into passive domain records or data classes to manually reconstruct displaced business rules, invariant checks, or state transitions that belong on the owning domain type or domain module.

no_message_chains.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Message Chains smell (Law of Demeter violations across behavior-bearing collaborators), without penalizing nested passive data reads or fluent pipelines on dot-count alone?

criteria.pass: Callers interact directly with their collaborators through intention-revealing operations rather than reaching through intermediate behavior-bearing collaborators to inspect or manipulate another owner's internals. Reading nested fields on passive data structures—such as nested documents, DTOs, read projections, state snapshots, event payloads, or configuration trees—and chaining fluent builders, standard collection transforms, or query pipelines do NOT fail for property-path or call-chain depth alone.
criteria.fail: Code repeatedly navigates through multiple behavior-bearing collaborators or service/domain handles (such as calling getters/accessors across several collaborating objects to reach into or mutate a distant owner's internal state or behavior) instead of exposing an intention-revealing operation on the intermediate collaborator. Nested property reads on passive data records, DTOs, projections, or configuration trees, and standard collection, builder, or query pipelines do NOT fail.

no_primitive_obsession.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Primitive Obsession smell, flagging only visibly unconstrained primitives rather than imported domain types, standalone boundary DTOs, or standard protocol/UI values?

criteria.pass: Constrained domain concepts, structured value groups, and shared semantic thresholds use dedicated types, unions/enums, or named constants rather than visibly unconstrained primitives, untyped tuples, or coupled behavioral boolean flag clusters. Literal comparisons against values typed by a named local or imported domain type (including fields or properties of imported domain types), union/enum, constant collection, or validation schema are NOT raw magic-string defects—treat imported domain types and their fields as properly constrained when their declarations live outside the supplied file. Standalone exported public API, request/response, contract, event, and boundary/storage DTO interfaces or records declaring plain primitive fields—including raw type/status strings and optional boolean input flags whose validation or domain parsing may live in another file or module—do NOT fail, and standard protocol, HTTP, markup/DOM, and parser fields/literals/status codes, independent UI or view-state flags, ordinary arithmetic and counts, timestamps/ISO strings, opaque IDs, and tokens/hashes remain acceptable as plain primitives.
criteria.fail: Core domain types or business logic in the supplied code visibly declare a constrained domain concept, state set, unit, or multi-field structure using unconstrained raw primitive types, untyped pairs/tuples, or coupled behavioral boolean control flags, OR repeat raw magic strings or unnamed domain thresholds/sentinels on unconstrained primitives where a shared named constant, union/enum, or value type belongs. Comparing values typed by an imported or local domain type (or its fields) against literal members, using plain primitives for standard protocol/HTTP fields and status codes, opaque IDs, ordinary counts, or independent UI state flags, or declaring standalone exported public API, request/response, contract, event, or boundary/storage DTO interfaces/records with plain primitive fields (including raw type/status strings and optional boolean input flags whose validation or domain parsing may live in another file or module) does NOT fail.

no_repeated_switches.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Repeated Switches smell?

criteria.pass: Conditional dispatch on a domain type, tier, or status is consolidated onto the owning enum/sealed hierarchy, lookup table, or a single authoritative location rather than repeated across multiple functions or classes. Local UI presentation rendering (such as rendering stage columns, badges, or labels for a single screen/view) and distinct lifecycle query predicates consolidated inside the owning domain module pass.
criteria.fail: Multiple `switch`/`when`/`if` chains across different operations, phases, methods, or files repeatedly branch on the same enum, status, or tier discriminant to implement scattered variant-specific rules.

no_speculative_or_middle_man.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Speculative Generality, Lazy Element, and Middle Man smells?

criteria.pass: Every class, interface, and wrapper earns its keep with a concrete responsibility required by the task, without unused extension points, speculative abstractions, or trivial pass-through delegates.
criteria.fail: The code contains speculative interfaces/abstractions for hypothetical future needs, near-empty types with no real responsibility, or middle-man classes whose methods merely forward calls unchanged to another object.

no_comment_deodorant_or_dead_code.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Comments-as-Deodorant and Dead Code smells?

criteria.pass: Comments are concise and purposeful—including brief doc-comments (such as short JSDoc, KDoc, or docstring summaries on exported modules, functions, types, or hooks explaining intent or contract) as well as non-obvious rationale, concurrency/locking intent, or contract nuances—rather than narrating obvious statements line by line or apologizing for convoluted code, and there is no commented-out code or unreachable private dead code.
criteria.fail: The code contains commented-out code blocks, unused or unreachable dead code (helpers, constants, or branches), noisy line-by-line narration restating obvious statements, or defensive deodorant comments excusing convoluted or hacky logic that should be refactored. Concise doc-comments summarizing the intent or contract of exported modules, functions, types, or hooks do NOT fail.
